description: Hello! I am building a passionate team for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. I am looking for members who are interested in programming, data analysis, web development, UI/UX design, or problem-solving. Whether you are a beginner or experienced, everyone is welcome! Our goal is to collaborate, learn, and build an awesome solution together. Join us!
summary:
Astro X is an interactive educational website created for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our project explores all machines that NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars, including rovers, landers, and scientific instruments. Instead of simply listing facts, we tell the stories behind these machines: why they were built, how they worked, what they discovered, and what happened to them.
We developed a searchable website that includes an interactive map and timeline, educational presentations, animations with voice-overs, and an interactive game. Visitors can explore space missions, discover important scientific achievements, and learn about the technology behind each machine.
Our project addresses the challenge by turning space exploration history into an engaging and easy-to-understand experience. It is important because these machines are more than abandoned equipment; they represent human curiosity, engineering achievements, and the scientific knowledge that continues to help us understand space.
details:
1. Our website allows visitors to explore machines that NASA sent to the Moon and Mars, including Surveyor landers and Opportunity rovers. Users can discover each machine's story through interactive slides, explore educational content, watch AI-generated videos with voice-over explanations, and test their understanding through interactive activities.

2. The main benefit of Astro X is that it transforms complex scientific and historical information into an accessible and engaging learning experience. Our goal is to increase students' curiosity about space, encourage independent learning, and help young people understand how previous missions contributed to our knowledge of the Moon and Mars.

3. What helped us boost the speed of creation was Claude which was used as helper in our progress, while the site was mainly built with HTML, CSS, JS, NodeJS, Sqlite3, and mainly VSCode as code editor.

4. We wanted to make our project creative by placing two online games, One which is free-play game-pool and the other Is competitive learning MCQ Questions Kahoot-like system, which gives good experience to students, and to avoid password-forgetting problems we made login/signup with Google Authenticator only.

5. Throughout development, our team considered scientific accuracy, simplicity of language, user experience, accessibility, visual design, and the needs of our target audience. We wanted to make the website useful for students with different levels of scientific knowledge.
